I am an American teen spending time as an exchange student in Denmark. AMA!
How obvious are the societal differences? Gun laws, Christianity, Islamaphobia, Marijuana use?

Gun laws; One of the first things I was asked (and am still asked quite often) is how many guns I own. I own none. Danes find it ridiculous how gun crazy the USA is. I have been here since August and have not seen a single gun (outside of guards at the royal palace).

Christianity; There isn't much of it. For the most part, people celebrate Christian holidays, but never attend services. My town has a single church, and out of the 10000 people, maybe 50 attend the church.

Islamaphobia; There's a lot of that. Denmark is full of immigrants coming from Islamic areas of the world, and Danes don't like it. They take jobs and don't pay taxes, and (in the Danes eyes) are the cause of what little crime Denmark has.

Marijuana use; A lot of that as well. It isn't legal, but it isn't enforced at all. People don't see smoking as a problem, and I haven't ever seen someone get arrested/fined for smoking here.
Is religion less significant as a whole? If so does it have an impact on people's open-mindedness? Such as on topics like evolution, abortion, gay marriage, or medical euthanasia.

Overall, religion doesn't really play a large part in society. The country as a whole is very liberal on topics such as gay marriage, abortion, and medical euthanasia. Evolution is accepted as fact 100%.

It's truly a culture thing. Kids dont really have curfews, they can go out and pretty much do whatever they want, drinking/partying or otherwise. That is mostly for teens, but I often see young kids (7-8) roaming the town by themselves without any real supervision.

I definitely do! I'm missing prom and graduation and all of those things so it does make me a bit sad at times. But I also know that this is a once in a lifetime opportunity. School is much more laid back here. Homework doesn't really exist, and it is a much more casual environment. The education is also some of the best in the world though, so just because we are relaxed doesn't mean we aren't learning!

Primarily, we speak Danish here. I am fluent in English (obviously), and near-fluent is Danish and Spanish.

I have to admit upfront that I am a bookaholic. I love to hold an actual book in my hands. I like the weight, the smell and being able to leaf back and forth through pages, marking them as I please. I have tried to like reading on a kindle or computer and it is just not the same for me. I have an entire 15 foot wall of floor to ceiling books and can't imagine life without them. lol
Do you prefer to read a real in your hand book or off of an electronic device?

I've only read one book on an electronic device, but I definitely enjoy the physical copy more. I like being able the weight of the pages shift from my right hand, to my left, as I progress through the book. There's also that great moment when you finish a chapter, and you glance at the clock and realize you should probably go to bed, but you still check and see how long the next chapter is, just in case it's a short one. It's just not the same on a device. Don't get me wrong, I'm not saying one is better than the other, it's just my personal preference.

I grew up with books. Physical paper books still win for me, but just barely. I love my kindle. It's well designed. If I hadn't grown up in the time before devices... it might easily be the other way around. Paper is... nostalgic. That's powerful.

I prefer digital.

Last year I digitized all of my old paperwork and downsized all of my old documents to a single, portable filing bin.

I then reduced my books to a single, half wall-height book shelf.

I plan to move within the next year however, so perhaps view physical books as holding an unnecessarily heavy cost.
Physical copies. With tablets/kindles, easy to get distracted while with books, I'm able to immerse myself into the story.

I really like the idea of everything kindle has to offer (and I still own my 1st or 2nd generation one) but I almost always choose the physical book over the ebook.

When I'm reading, oftentimes I like to flip back to reread something from a previous chapter. Perhaps there was a particular phrase that didn't seem important at the time but something in a later chapter connects with it and I want to refresh my memory on the specific wording. Or sometimes I realize I kinda spaced out for a few minutes and I want to skim over what I just "read". With a physical book I don't find myself pulled out of the story when I use my index finger to keep my place and thumb backwards across the pages to find what I'm looking for but on my kindle doing so feels clunky and time-consuming.

I also like seeing how much of the book is left. Maybe it's sort of a visual accomplishment. The little progress bar on the kindle doesn't give me the same satisfaction though I couldn't say why not.

I really want to love my kindle. On paper (or e-ink if you will haha) its benefits far outweigh the disadvantages but in practice, an old fashioned book makes reading feel more interactive to me. That being said, if tomorrow all the book publishers of the world decided they were never going to print another book on paper, I would happily pick up the kindle as my only option and I'm sure eventually I would come to enjoy it as much as the "classic" experience.
Electronic. I like the idea of books but god are they clunky to actually read. I'd rather read on my phone or on my kindle to be perfectly honest.
Both. Depends on my mood. And the book. I do like the search capabilities and ease of quoting by copy and paste of ebooks.
I prefer actual books; reading stuff from my computer screen causes me eyestrain.

I love the look of bookshelves so when I'm older I must have a library. Full of all my favorite books that I like to reread but for now I like my ereader. I currently have 228 books on it and I take it everywhere so it's nice to literally have a library on me at all times.

I also have a tablet that I use to read comics on but that's it though. I don't really like to read books on it. The e-ink is the key to reading off an ereader. It's just softer on the eyes.
I can read faster with a book in my hand. It's just easier for me to manage vs my phone or a tablet.
I like to read the first 40 pages or so of a book on my ereader to see if I like it before I buy it. But if I had to choose between the two, I'd pick paper every time.

I prefer my phone/PC to paper typically for a variety of reasons:

  • The most important is that I have my phone with me almost all the time anyway, so If I want to read I don't have to carry something else with me or remember to bring a book, I can leave the house without knowing whether I'll have spare time to read and still be prepared to do so. I can even buy and download books on the spot if my library is insufficient.

  • I can carry my whole library (or all of it that I own digitally anyway) with me, and I don't need to store/move a load of books all the time.

  • Various "nice to have" features are available on my phone/PC and not with a paper book such as: not seeing the page counter so you don't know if the book is almost over, adjusting the color/brightness/size/contrast of text to my liking, automatic bookmarking, easy/fast chapter skipping, a search function, easy to read at night no matter where you are (no separate awkward light needed), built-in highlighting, and the ability to instantly look up words I'm unfamiliar with or that are in another language.

  • No paper cuts

The main downside is battery life if you're on a phone of course, but I rarely find myself in a situation where this is an issue, and the benefits for me vastly outweigh the drawbacks. I have some nostalgia from spending a considerable part of my life reading from paper, but not enough to go back unless an electronic version in unavailable.

I prefer reading off a tablet device such as my Kindle Fire or iPad Mini. I love having internet access to download more free ebooks offered on websites such as Gutenberg, Manybooks, and Feedbooks directly onto my device. The storage is another benefit, I have nearly three thousand books spanning both devices.

The dimensions and weight of a real book are just a drain on available space. I've been in the process of moving for the past week and this included having to manually move my private library (~400 books). I love books... but damn. It had me meditating on the issue and I realized that the benefits of having an actual book are nothing in comparison to its consequences. For one, you can only read so many at one time and all that are not in use are just dead weight. The same argument can't be made about electronic storage, because an ebook tends to be within 50 to 500 KBs at the most and the memory itself is within the GBs.

I'm not about to purge my current library in favor of my reading devices, but I will definitely make it a point to find an electronic copy of a book rather than physical in the future.

I tend to go back and forth.

If I am on vacation and enjoying a book I want the real thing in my hands. There is just something more relaxing that way.

If I am reading a book while I go about my day-to-day life it is just more convenient to read off my phone/tablet/reader so I tend to use the amazon Kindle app. The only thing I do not like about reading off my phone/tablet is that most people assume I'm just another young person glued to technology and have no appreciation for life around me because I'm staring at my screen all day. Little do they know i'm reading Dante's Inferno and the Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave

While an electronic device has it's advantages (i.e. not having to move 50 lbs of books across the country 3 times) I will never be able to give up everything that makes a physical book special. There's just something about looking at my shelves full of books and remembering everything that made each one special to me. Opening up a book that I haven't read in years, and having everything that was happening in that time of my life come rushing back is a feeling I don't think I will ever get with an ebook. Mostly because I used the same tablet for more than just reading.
